verdict.rationale: Gitea's own Gitea Actions feature lets developers write CI/CD workflows in YAML that are compatible with GitHub Actions, and Gitea ships an official action runner. That covers the pipelines-as-code core of the story. However, the evidence never explicitly documents workflows living in the repository or triggering automatically on pushes and pull requests; this is only implied by GitHub Actions syntax compatibility. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of in-repo workflow files and push/PR triggers, and independent hands-on corroboration of Gitea Actions running.

support.subject: As a developer, I can define CI/CD pipelines as code in my repository and have them run automatically on pushes and pull requests

citations.quote: Gitea Actions supports CI/CD functionality, compatible with GitHub Actions. Users can write workflows in familiar YAML format and reuse a variety of existing Actions plugins.
Workflow and action syntax is compatible with GitHub Actions.
We provide an official go-sdk, a CLI tool called tea and an action runner for Gitea Action.
Reuse thousands of existing GitHub Actions inside your Gitea instances.
